key_insight: IdeaAnchor shows that LLMs can be taught to generate research ideas directly from literature by using structured specifications as supervision, instead of relying only on prompts or feedback. This makes ideation more grounded, controllable, and aligned with how humans synthesize papers into new directions.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the difficulty of training language models to turn a set of related research papers into novel, literature-grounded ideas. Existing prompting- and feedback-based methods do not provide enough structured guidance for how papers should be synthesized into meaningful research directions.
method: Introduces IdeaAnchor, a training paradigm that uses structured specifications as privileged signals for literature-based ideation.
Teaches the model to synthesize evidence across papers and map that synthesis into a research idea generation process.
Provides a more explicit supervision signal than standard prompting, improving the model’s ability to produce grounded and organized ideas.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a practical path toward models that can assist with literature review and early-stage research brainstorming. It may improve research productivity by helping users discover gaps, connect related work, and generate more plausible novel directions.
